knowledge:
- key_parameters: min_sens=Minimum sensitivity requirement for the binary classifier (e.g., 0.95) ;; min_spec=Minimum specificity requirement for the binary classifier (e.g., 0.85) ;; obj_func=The objective function used in survival mode to quantify the difference in survival times between groups ('tau', 'reltau', or 'coxcoef') ;; obj_min=The minimum value of the survival objective function that all classifiers must satisfy on a test cohort ;; parallel=Logical indicating whether to run calculations in parallel (highly recommended for large datasets in messinaSurv) ;; silent=Logical to suppress progress messages during fitting ;; seed=Random seed for reproducibility of bootstrap resampling
- alternatives: Conventional multi-feature classifiers (like SVM or kNN) which do not restrict the number of features and are hard to translate to single-gene clinical assays ;; Classical statistical tests (like the t-test) which work on a per-feature basis but are not designed for classification and lose power in the presence of expression outliers
- when_to_use: Use when you want to identify single-gene biomarkers for clinical translation (e.g., developing a low-cost qPCR or immunohistochemistry diagnostic/prognostic test) ;; Use when analyzing clinical datasets with high sample heterogeneity, potential experimental outliers, or undiscovered sample subtypes
- pitfalls: Running messinaSurv on large datasets without parallel processing (parallel = FALSE) can result in extremely long runtimes ;; Using 'reltau' or 'coxcoef' objective functions in survival analysis can lead to unstable fits compared to the more stable 'tau' objective, especially if the cohort contains very unbalanced subgroups

workflows.name: binary_classification_messina
workflows.intent: Construct optimal single-gene threshold classifiers to distinguish between two distinct sample classes (e.g., normal vs. tumor).
input: expression_matrix.csv (matrix of continuous gene expression values with genes as rows and samples as columns)
sample_metadata.csv (table containing binary class labels for each sample)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the expression data and class labels ;; 2. Subset the data to the two classes of interest ;; 3. Fit the Messina classification model using the messina function with specified sensitivity and specificity thresholds ;; 4. Inspect the S4 result object to identify features passing performance requirements ;; 5. Plot the classifier fits, thresholds, and margins using the plot function
workflows.code:
library(messina)
library(antiProfilesData)
data(apColonData)
x = exprs(apColonData)
y = pData(apColonData)$SubType
sel = y %in% c("normal", "tumor")
x = x[,sel]
y = y[sel]
fit.apColon = messina(x, y == "tumor", min_sens = 0.95, min_spec = 0.85, seed = 1234, silent = TRUE)
fit.apColon
plot(fit.apColon, i = 1, plot_type = "point")
plot(fit.apColon, i = c(1,2,10,50), plot_type = "point")

workflows.name: survival_analysis_messina
workflows.intent: Identify optimal single-gene threshold classifiers to predict survival outcomes and separate patients into short and long survivors.
input: expression_matrix.csv (matrix of continuous gene expression values with genes as rows and samples as columns)
survival_data.csv (table containing survival times and censoring status for each sample)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the expression data and survival times ;; 2. Create a Surv object representing survival times and censoring status ;; 3. Fit the Messina survival model using the messinaSurv function with a specified objective function and minimum value ;; 4. Inspect the S4 result object to identify features passing performance requirements ;; 5. Plot the survival curves and separation at the threshold and margins using the plot function
workflows.code:
library(messina)
library(survival)
data(tcga_kirc_example)
dim(kirc.exprs)
kirc.surv
fit.surv = messinaSurv(kirc.exprs, kirc.surv, obj_func = "tau", obj_min = 0.6, parallel = FALSE, silent = TRUE)
fit.surv
plot(fit.surv, bootstrap_type = "ci")
